analysis.investment_thesis: Alivus (formerly Glenmark Life Sciences) is a near debt-free API business with excellent 31% operating margins and 23% ROCE, qualities I deeply respect. However, at 37x trailing P/E with FCF yield of only ~1.7% (FCF INR 225 Cr vs market cap INR 13,128 Cr), the price is too generous for my comfort — I wait for businesses to come to me at reasonable prices.
key_strengths: Fortress balance sheet — D/E of just 0.02 with only INR 57 Cr debt against INR 2,817 Cr equity
Exceptional operating margins of 31.45% with consistent EBITDA expansion from INR 267 Cr (2019) to INR 711 Cr (2025)
High promoter holding at 74.87% and virtually zero finance costs (INR 2 Cr) signal management discipline
key_risks: Revenue growth has effectively stalled post-2022 — only ~4% CAGR from INR 2,087 Cr (2022) to INR 2,340 Cr (2025), well below the 6-year 17.6% headline CAGR
Large unexplained investing outflow of INR 616 Cr in FY2025 (vs INR 116 Cr in FY2024) drained cash from INR 301 Cr to INR 71 Cr — purpose unclear
API segment has inherent pricing commoditization risk, and Nirma takeover from Glenmark adds strategic uncertainty during transition
red_flags: FCF yield of ~1.7% is far below my 5% threshold — investor is paying a full price for future earnings that haven't yet materialized
FY2025 investing CF of -616 Cr against operating CF of only 392 Cr — cash is being deployed faster than it is earned; needs clarification on nature of investment
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Alivus has the balance sheet I admire — essentially zero debt, self-funding growth, and consistent OCF positive across all four reported years. The operating margin of 31.45% and ROCE of 23.3% tell me this is a genuinely good business with pricing power in specialty APIs like olmesartan, sitagliptin, and rosuvastatin. The 6-year profit CAGR of 16.3% is in my preferred range, and the promoter (now Nirma) holding of 74.87% is reassuring. These are businesses I can understand and respect.

However, I am troubled by the price and recent momentum. At 37x trailing earnings, Mr. Market is asking me to pay for perfection — but the last three years show revenue growing at only ~4% CAGR. Free cash flow has compressed from INR 465 Cr in FY2022 to INR 225 Cr in FY2025. The sudden INR 616 Cr investing outflow in FY2025 — nearly five times the prior year — without a clear acquisition announcement is a flag I cannot ignore. I do not invest in what I do not understand. The forward P/E of 21x suggests the market expects a sharp earnings re-rating, but I have not seen the revenue acceleration to justify that confidence. I will watch this patiently and revisit if it corrects to below 22x trailing earnings.
